## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1,\ j=r-t+1,\ a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\ b=\min(i,j)\); the lower-adjoined family generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- claim-2: The transposed/right-adjoined family is \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), and is the conjugate family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- claim-3: In the \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,3)\) interval, the ten lower-adjoined classes form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q=J/A_+J\). [artifact 527b9b1cd586e81294f01def5f51d30afb4c5919e505f335d85bd759ec0facf1; artifact fe0114a78a3f2045e7b37abfb47b72bebb85782ac6dc52bc0b3bcf6ce46b3e14]
- claim-4: Partition conjugation induces an automorphism of \(Q\), preserves \(A_+J\), and carries the certified lower-adjoined basis to the right-adjoined family.
- claim-5: Both specialized ten-element families minimally generate \(J\).
## Strategy
For \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,3)\), take \(n=10,r=s=5,t=4\); then \(a=3,b=2\). Partition conjugation \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) preserves \(I_{5,5}\), since \(5^5\) is self-conjugate, and hence descends to \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\). It preserves
\[
J=\bigoplus_{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^5}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda,
\]
because \(22'=22\). Since \(\omega\) preserves degrees, \(\omega(A_+)=A_+\), and therefore
\[
\omega(A_+J)=A_+J.
\]
Thus \(\omega\) induces an involution of \(Q=J/A_+J\).

The accepted exact computation certifies that the lower-adjoined family
\[
\{\bar s_{22},\bar s_{221},\bar s_{222},\bar s_{2211},\bar s_{2221},
\bar s_{2222},\bar s_{22111},\bar s_{22211},\bar s_{22221},\bar s_{22222}\}
\]
is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\). Its conjugate is exactly
\[
\{\bar s_{22},\bar s_{32},\bar s_{33},\bar s_{42},\bar s_{43},
\bar s_{44},\bar s_{52},\bar s_{53},\bar s_{54},\bar s_{55}\},
\]
the right-adjoined family \(22\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^2\). Hence this family is also a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\).

The lower family generates \(J\) by the specialized source theorem [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]; applying \(\omega\) gives generation by the right family. The accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion therefore implies that both ten-element families are irredundant, hence minimally generate \(J\).

Thus the requested target is established for this specific \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,3)\) case.

## Gaps
No gap for this case-specific conclusion. This does not establish arbitrary cases with \(p=c=3\).
